title: Contextual Access Insights: Workspace-level RBAC microflows & audit trail UX
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, contextual RBAC surface inside the Redwood Console workspace header and audit timeline that helps admins understand who has access, why, and recent access changes without switching pages. Deliver hi-fi prototypes for a workspace-level Access Insights panel and an inline Audit Microflow for approving/revoking temporary access.
problem_statement: Admins and platform engineers waste time navigating between the Teams, Roles, and Audit Log pages to answer simple questions: who can access this route, when was access changed, and can I quickly remediate a questionable grant? Current console flows scatter information across dashboards and bulk CSV exports, causing triage delays during incidents and audits.
goals: Provide quick, contextual answers at the workspace level: 'who can do X' and 'when did Y change'
Enable one-click remediation (revoke, temporary revoke, request justification) from the same surface
Surface explainability for role membership derived from group policies and inheritance
Minimize cognitive load for non-security admins through progressive disclosure
constraints: Must respect existing RBAC data model and not introduce new server calls beyond a single aggregated API per workspace
Design should be implementable within the current console layout and theming (no major nav rework)
Audit trail entries are immutable; UX should not imply editability but should support contextual response actions
proposed_screens: Workspace header Access pill (summary counts + quick filter)
Access Insights panel (roles, derived permissions, last changed, source-of-truth link)
Audit Microflow slide-over: selected event details, related grants, one-click revoke/temporary-revoke, request justification modal
Access timeline compact view with faceted filtering (actor, role, permission, time range)
Onboarding coachmark explaining temporary access flow and audit provenance
decisions: Aggregate API will return permission derivation strings (e.g., 'via group: infra-ops') instead of full policy objects to keep payload small
Inline revoke will queue a server-side 'revoke request' to preserve audit immutability and allow rollback via existing admin workflows
Temporary-revoke will default to 24 hours with dropdown presets (1h, 8h, 24h, 7d) and require justification for >=24h
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates access summary in workspace header and opens panel with no more than two clicks
Audit Microflow slide-over shows event context, related grants, and exposes actions (revoke, temp-revoke, request-justification)
Design files include responsive variants for 1024px+ and 768px widths
Hand-off tokens and component specs documented in the Figma file and a short CSS variables sheet
Usability session with 5 admin users completed and no more than 2 critical usability issues
tasks: Design low-fi flows for discoverability and remediation (Maya)
Build hi-fi Figma prototype and component specs (Rafael)
Sync with infra/serving for aggregated API contract (Soren Li)
Create acceptance test checklist and recruit participants for usability study (Anya Patel)
Write design handoff notes and add to PR description for front-end implementation (Rafael)
